subject: english
fullTitle: Unit 1: Advanced Prose Analysis & Critical Reading
loDesc: Reads complex prose texts critically to analyze authorial voice, deduce implicit subtext, evaluate character arcs, and master high-level contextual vocabulary.
hookDemo: Display two short literary excerpts describing a trial scene: one written with detached legal objectivity, the other written with emotional bias.
hookAsk: How does an author's narrative point of view shape reader sympathy and moral judgment?
streamDo: Observe 5 highlighted advanced vocabulary words within a 200-word literary passage.
streamTask: Match given contextual vocabulary words with their correct synonyms and identify the tone of the passage (Irony, Sarcasm, Nostalgia, Melancholy).
mountainTask: Read a given story excerpt, analyze the protagonist's moral transformation in a 120-word paragraph, and cite 2 pieces of textual evidence.
skyTask: Synthesize how two different short stories present the conflict between 'Individual Ambition vs Social Duty' in a 150-word analytical essay.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing a narrator's subjective personal opinion with the author's overall objective message or theme.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Is the first-person narrator reliable, or is the author using irony to show the narrator's flaws?'

crossCurricularLinks: Ethics & Philosophy: Moral Dilemmas (Evaluating individual ambition vs civic responsibility in literary prose)

metaNcertCode: Secondary English LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 14]
metaNcertDesc: Reads prose critically to analyze character transformations, authorial style, and thematic subtext.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Pedagogy Note: Organize socratic circle discussions to evaluate character motives.

subject: english
fullTitle: Unit 2: Poetic Structure, Devices & Critical Appreciation
loDesc: Analyzes complex poetic structures, evaluates literary devices (Oxymoron, Paradox, Symbolism, Irony, Transferred Epithet, Metaphor), and drafts comprehensive appreciations.
hookDemo: Recite two famous poetic phrases: 'deafening silence' and 'sleepless night'.
hookAsk: What is the difference between an Oxymoron (contradictory terms paired) and a Transferred Epithet (adjective shifted to another noun)?
streamDo: Observe lines from prescribed Grade 10 poems.
streamTask: Classify given poem lines under Symbolism, Oxymoron, Paradox, Irony, or Transferred Epithet.
mountainTask: Write a 5-point critical appreciation of a prescribed poem covering: Title, Poet, Rhyme Scheme, Figures of Speech, and Central Philosophical Theme.
skyTask: Compose an original 4-line stanza on 'Time' incorporating an ABAB rhyme scheme, one Symbolism, and one Oxymoron.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing Transferred Epithet with Personification (e.g. assuming 'sleepless night' means the night itself is alive and awake).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Who is actually sleepless—the person or the night?' The adjective 'sleepless' is transferred from person to night.

crossCurricularLinks: Aesthetics & Philosophy: Symbolic Imagery (Decoding abstract philosophical undertones in poetic verse)

metaNcertCode: Secondary English LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 14]
metaNcertDesc: Appreciates advanced poetic forms, complex literary devices, and philosophical undertones.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Pedagogy Note: Use poetry slam recitations to explore meter and cadence.

subject: english
loDesc: Transforms sentences (Simple, Compound, Complex; Degrees of Comparison; Affirmative/Negative), applies Clause synthesis, and masters Subject-Verb Concord in formal writing.
hookDemo: Display a simple sentence: 'In spite of being poor, he is honest.'
hookAsk: How do we convert this into a Compound sentence using 'but' and a Complex sentence using 'although'?
streamTask: Transform given simple sentences into compound and complex sentence structures without changing meaning.
mountainTask: Transform the sentence 'Iron is more useful than any other metal' into Positive and Superlative degrees of comparison.
skyTask: Synthesize 6 short choppy sentences into a single cohesive 3-sentence paragraph using relative clauses and subordinating conjunctions.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Altering the core meaning of a sentence when converting from Positive to Comparative/Superlative degree.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Does "Iron is the most useful metal" mean the same as "No other metal is as useful as iron"?' Maintain precise meaning balance.

crossCurricularLinks: Linguistic Logic & Syntax: Structural Editing (Synthesizing complex clause relationships for academic writing)

metaNcertCode: Secondary English LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 14]
metaNcertDesc: Transforms sentence structures, synthesizes clauses, and applies subject-verb concord in context.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Pedagogy Note: Use sentence-combining games to build structural fluency.

subject: english
fullTitle: Unit 4: Formal Correspondence: Editorial & Municipal Complaints
loDesc: Composes formal letters to newspaper editors, civic authorities, and business managers regarding social, environmental, and consumer issues following standard block layouts.
hookDemo: Display a formal letter to an Editor side by side with a Consumer Court complaint letter.
hookAsk: What structural elements differ in tone, reference numbers, and call to action between editorial and consumer complaints?
streamDo: Observe mixed phrases: 'I want you to fix this ASAP', 'I am writing to draw your kind attention to...', 'Thanks a lot', 'Yours faithfully'.
streamTask: Classify phrases into Appropriate Formal Register versus Inappropriate Informal Phrasing.
mountainTask: Write a formal letter (120-150 words) to the Editor of a national daily raising concern over reckless driving and inadequate traffic enforcement near school zones.
skyTask: Draft a formal letter of complaint (120-150 words) to the Store Manager regarding a defective laptop purchased recently, demanding replacement under warranty.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Demanding direct municipal action from a newspaper Editor instead of asking the Editor to publish the issue to draw public authority attention.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Can a newspaper editor fix road potholes directly, or do they publish your letter to alert municipal officers?'

crossCurricularLinks: Civics & Consumer Protection: Legal Redressal (Drafting formal consumer complaint letters citing warranty terms and consumer rights)

metaNcertCode: Secondary English LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 14]
metaNcertDesc: Writes formal letters, editorial letters, and business complaint letters adhering to standard block conventions.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Pedagogy Note: Use real local civic problems from newspapers as authentic letter prompts.

subject: english
fullTitle: Unit 5: Creative Writing: Narrative & Analytical Paragraphs
loDesc: Drafts analytical paragraphs based on given data charts/graphs and writes original creative narratives with well-developed plots, character motivations, and resolutions.
hookDemo: Display a pie chart showing reading habits among teenagers across 3 genres (Fiction 45%, Non-fiction 30%, Comics 25%).
hookAsk: How do we write an objective analytical paragraph summarizing key data trends without injecting personal bias?
streamDo: Observe data trend phrases: 'Increased sharply', 'Remained steady', 'In stark contrast to', 'Peak value'.
streamTask: Classify phrases under Comparison, Trend Description, or Data Highlighting categories.
mountainTask: Write a 120-word analytical paragraph summarizing data trends from a given bar graph showing annual energy consumption across sectors.
skyTask: Write an original short story (150-200 words) based on the opening prompt: 'The old key fit perfectly into the rusted lock, but what lay inside was completely unexpected...', incorporating dialogue and a clear climax.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Injecting personal opinions or speculative reasons ('Teenagers read fiction because comics are boring') into an analytical paragraph based on data graphs.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Is that speculative opinion stated in the graph, or are you inferring beyond the provided data?' Stick strictly to graph facts.

crossCurricularLinks: Statistics & Data Science: Data Interpretation (Summarizing statistical bar charts and pie graphs into concise prose)

metaNcertCode: Secondary English LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 14]
metaNcertDesc: Writes analytical paragraphs from data visualizers and composes creative narratives using rich plots.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Pedagogy Note: Practice interpreting bar charts and pie graphs verbally before drafting analytical paragraphs.

subject: english
fullTitle: Unit 6: Persuasive Writing: Speeches & Debate Motions
loDesc: Drafts persuasive speeches for public assemblies and structures rigorous debate arguments (FOR/AGAINST) on contemporary socio-economic and scientific topics.
hookDemo: Display a debate motion: 'Online education can completely replace traditional classroom schooling.'
hookAsk: What rhetorical strategies (facts, emotional appeal, logical reasoning) make a debate speaker persuasive?
streamDo: Observe speech excerpts using Rhetorical Questions, Repetition, Rule of Three, and Direct Address.
streamTask: Identify rhetorical devices used in given speech excerpts on your worksheet.
mountainTask: Write a 150-word persuasive speech on 'Sustainable Living: The Imperative Choice for Youth' to be delivered in morning assembly.
skyTask: Compose a 150-word debate speech arguing FOR or AGAINST the motion: 'Automated AI tools will benefit human creativity rather than destroy it', including a strong rebuttal.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Presenting both FOR and AGAINST arguments within a single debate speech instead of taking a decisive, well-supported stance on one side.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Are you assigned to argue FOR or AGAINST the motion?' Stick firmly to one side while refuting the opposite.

crossCurricularLinks: Social Sciences & Policy: Parliamentary Debate (Constructing persuasive arguments and evidence-based policy speeches)

metaNcertCode: Secondary English LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 14]
metaNcertDesc: Drafts persuasive speeches and debate arguments using logical structure and rhetorical devices.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Pedagogy Note: Conduct mock parliamentary debates in class to build public speaking confidence.
